doc.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018

title: Spirituality in his playing; first hearing Charice
summary: Spirituality comes out in his saxophone; he describes weeping on hearing singer Charice.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Does it come out in your saxophone?

Oh yeah. Um hum. I can’t brag but when people heard me when I was younger, some people were touched, other people like Leonard Feather said I sounded like a wet noodle one day, so it could have hurt my feelings. But like when I play “Over the Rainbow” for example, a lot of times people cry. I’ve never cried that I remember for Charlie Parker. I mean, these are the great, and Coltrane. The only other time I’ve cried, to be honest, and I won’t go into a big thing about this because my wife would, I don’t want to drive her crazy. But I heard this young pop singer. I don’t follow pop anymore. I’m more of a jazz person. But I’ve done all that stuff you know, at whatever level. But I heard this girl Charice. You ever hear of her? She’s from the Philippines. I heard her when she was fifteen, eight years ago. I’m almost crying now. I hear her I start to cry. I have never heard anybody sing pop, at any age, all famous people, sing as good as her.
